annotations.betterLine: Cast Faithless Looting for {R} (via Raucous Theater), draw 2 and discard 2, then cast Psychic Frog for {U}{B} (via Watery Grave + Swamp). This maximizes mana usage, deploys the stronger threat, and fuels the graveyard for Psychic Frog's abilities.

annotations.description: Casting Emperor of Bones before playing a land drop (Scalding Tarn) is a sequencing error. Playing Scalding Tarn first costs nothing and provides additional information and flexibility - it could be cracked for a Mountain to cast Faithless Looting, or held as an additional mana source. Additionally, casting Psychic Frog (UB) might be slightly better here since it's an evasive threat that draws cards on combat damage, and the graveyard currently has very few creatures to exile with Emperor of Bones. However, the land-before-spell sequencing is the clearest mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Emperor of Bones before playing a land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Scalding Tarn first, then decide between casting Emperor of Bones or Psychic Frog with full information and maximum mana available.

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones exiles a card from a graveyard, and when +1/1 counters are placed on it (via Adapt), it can put an exiled creature card onto the battlefield. Exiling Snapback (an instant) means it can never be reanimated by Emperor of Bones. Goblin Charbelcher is an artifact, also not a creature. However, the key consideration is denying the opponent resources. Goblin Charbelcher is a much more dangerous card for the opponent to potentially recur or interact with - it's a powerful artifact that could win the game. Snapback is a relatively low-impact bounce spell that's already been used. More importantly, neither card exiled here is a creature, so neither can be reanimated by Emperor of Bones. The choice doesn't matter much for Emperor's reanimation ability, but exiling Goblin Charbelcher would deny the opponent a potentially game-winning artifact if they have any graveyard recursion (like Tameshi, Reality Architect, which can return artifacts from graveyard to battlefield).
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Snapback from opponent's graveyard with Emperor of Bones trigger
annotations.betterLine: Exile Goblin Charbelcher from opponent's graveyard to deny potential recursion of a much more powerful card, especially given cards like Tameshi or Whir of Invention that the opponent might be building toward

annotations.description: Fetching basic Island instead of Steam Vents. While Island provides untapped blue, Steam Vents would provide both blue AND red from one land, giving better mana flexibility for a deck running both Psychic Frog (UB) and Faithless Looting (R). The 2 life cost at 15 life is very manageable.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched basic Island with Scalding Tarn
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Steam Vents (paying 2 life) for better color flexibility, providing access to both U and R from one land while still enabling Psychic Frog next turn

annotations.description: Emperor of Bones already has +1/+1 counters on it, so Adapt 2 does nothing — Adapt only adds counters if the creature has no +1/+1 counters. This wastes 2 mana ({1}{B}) for zero effect. The player should have recognized that their 4/4 Emperor of Bones with 2 +1/+1 counters cannot be adapted again.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Adapt 2 on Emperor of Bones that already had two +1/+1 counters, wasting 2 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Play Scalding Tarn as a land drop, then cast Psychic Frog ({U}{B}) to develop the board, or cast Faithless Looting to dig for cards. The 2 mana spent on a failed Adapt was completely wasted.

annotations.description: Cast Psychic Frog before playing Scalding Tarn from hand. annotations.actionTaken: Cast Psychic Frog (UB) before making land drop with Scalding Tarn
annotations.betterLine: Play Scalding Tarn first, then cast Psychic Frog, leaving more mana available for other plays this turn

annotations.description: Fetched Watery Grave which provides U/B colors already available, when Blood Crypt would have provided access to R mana needed to cast Faithless Looting in hand. Faithless Looting is a key enabler for the Emperor of Bones graveyard strategy.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Watery Grave (U/B), duplicating existing color coverage
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Blood Crypt (B/R) to enable casting Faithless Looting next turn, which fuels the graveyard for Emperor of Bones and digs for more resources

annotations.description: Cast Fallaji Archaeologist (0/3, mills 3) instead of Tameshi, Reality Architect (2/3) with the Lotus Bloom's 3 mana. Tameshi is a better body and critically can recover Goblin Charbelcher from the graveyard in future turns, which is the player's win condition. With no lands on board, the player is in a desperate position where setting up the Charbelcher recovery plan via Tameshi is more important than milling 3 cards.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Tameshi, Reality Architect to set up future Goblin Charbelcher recovery from graveyard and get a better body on board
